headline: Sleep debt is today's real limiter — readiness looks moderate on paper, but 26h of accumulated deficit means the easy run needs to actually be easy.
body_state: Readiness composite 61.5/100 (moderate band), but the verdict flags **sleep** as the driver, not the score: 26h of 14-day sleep debt, last night only 6.3h (sleep score 66). Garmin's own training readiness reads lower — 52, status **Recovery**. HRV 45ms, BALANCED. Body battery recovered well overnight (+44) but sits at 47 now. Stress is low (avg 15) — the deficit is sleep quantity, not daytime load. Overtraining composite is green; this isn't a red-flag day, it's a protect-the-margin one.
session: Plan calls for a 7km easy run @ 4:50-5:19/km. You've already banked 46min of Un1t this morning — 69.7% of it in zone 3 (avg HR 132, peak 163, right at your LTHR) — a real stimulus before this run even starts. Run this one genuinely easy: HR under ~130, pace toward the slow edge (5:00+/km) rather than the 4:20s you've been drifting to on 'easy' days. Grey-zone training is your #1 ranked limiter (17.8% true easy vs an 80% target) — today's a chance to bank a real easy day. Hold cadence 168-172 spm.
recent: Aug 7's progressive long run closed at 179bpm/RPE 8 — readiness cratered to 23 the next day. Aug 8's Un1t landed green vs plan (42min, HR 130). Aug 10's 'easy' run ran 89.7% in zone 3 at 4:27/km, HR 136 — same pattern as this morning's Un1t. The thread: intensity keeps creeping into days meant to be easy, and readiness has whiplashed (11→52→61.5) this week paying for it. Cadence has held steady 155-160 spm across these sessions — still under the 168-172 target.
focus: Run today's 7km genuinely easy — HR under 130, slow the pace, protect against the grey-zone limiter
